title: Cap. 1 vocabulary: Praedestinatio — dual use; school sense
pass_a_gloss: I come therefore to the vocabulary of Predestination, which sometimes, though rarely, is used by theologians even in a bad part, namely for destination unto death. So Augustine, Tractate 48 on John: How, he says, did he say to those, You are not from my sheep? because he was seeing them predestined unto everlasting destruction, not compared unto eternal life by the price of his blood. And City of God 15 chapter 1. He says there are two cities or societies of human beings; of which one is predestined to reign forever with God, the other to undergo eternal punishment with the devil. So also Augustine's disciples Prosper and Fulgentius sometimes speak. Moreover the Fathers in the Council of Valence confess the predestination of the elect unto life, and the predestination of the impious unto death. But we (which has now nearly obtained in the School of the Theologians) narrow the vocabularies of predestination and of the predestined unto that special providence of God by which from eternity he proposed to procure by efficacious means the salvation of those whom he elected in Christ: and conformably to this eternal purpose, he efficaciously and infallibly works their salvation in time.
pass_b_english: I turn next to Predestination. Theologians sometimes — though rarely — use that word for a bad end too: destination to death. So Augustine on John, Tractate 48: How did he say to them, "You are not of my sheep"? Because he saw them predestined to everlasting ruin, not purchased for eternal life by the price of his blood. And in City of God 15.1 he says there are two cities or societies of human beings: one predestined to reign forever with God, the other to suffer eternal punishment with the devil. Augustine's disciples Prosper and Fulgentius sometimes speak the same way. The Fathers at the Council of Valence even confess a predestination of the elect to life and a predestination of the ungodly to death. We, following what has nearly become school usage, narrow "predestination" and "the predestined" to that special providence of God by which from eternity he proposed to secure, by efficacious means, the salvation of those he chose in Christ — and, matching that eternal purpose, he works their salvation in time efficaciously and without fail.
source_text: Venio igitur ad vocabulum Praedestinationis, quod aliquando, licet raro, in malam etiam partem usurpatur a Theologis, nimirum pro destinatione ad mortem. Sic Augustinus Tract. 48. in Johan.: Quomodo, inquit, istis dixit, Non estis ex ovibus meis? quia videbat eos ad sempiternum interitum praedestinatos, non ad vitam aeternam sui sanguinis pretio comparatos. Et 15. De civit. cap. 1. Duo dicit esse civitates vel societates hominum; quarum una praedestinata est in aeternum regnare cum Deo, altera aeternum supplicium subire cum diabolo. Sic etiam nonnunquam loquuntur Augustini discipuli, Prosper, & Fulgentius. Quinetiam Patres in Concilio Valentino confitentur praedestinationem electorum ad vitam, & praedestinationem impiorum ad mortem. Sed nos (quod jam fere obtinuit in Schola Theologorum) praedestinationis & praedestinatorum vocabula arctamus ad illam providentiam Dei specialem, qua ab aeterno proposuit illorum salutem efficacibus mediis procurare, quos in Christo elegit: & conformiter huic aeterno proposito, eorundem salutem in tempore efficaciter & infallibiliter operatur.
